themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1500% increase (z-score: 8.66)—suggesting either rapid deterioration of street conditions or a sudden operational failure by Sanitation.
evidence: 4 street sweeping complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (1500% spike, z-score 8.66)
Spike is most recent data point and represents abrupt acceleration
Street Condition is already a top 311 category (856 complaints over 90 days), suggesting broader infrastructure issue
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation to identify what triggered the spike—staffing shortage, route changes, equipment issues, or weather?
Walk affected blocks identified in 311 complaints and document visible debris/conditions
Interview residents about how street cleanliness has changed in past 2 weeks

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from parks jumped to 5 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.5 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 900% spike (z-score: 6.36)—indicating a sudden change in park use, events, or enforcement.
evidence: 5 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (900% increase, z-score 6.36)
Signal is most recent in dataset; represents brand-new trend
Jackson Heights / Elmhurst has multiple parks; spike suggests neighborhood-wide issue, not isolated incident
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are generating complaints via 311 data; visit those locations during evening/weekend hours to observe activity
Interview Parks Department about any new permitted events, summer programming changes, or staffing at Jackson Heights or Elmhurst parks
Talk to residents adjacent to parks about what changed—illegal gatherings, vendor activity, construction, or legitimate recreation expansion?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 4 approximately 3 weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 3100% increase (z-score: 11.72)—suggesting a major graffiti, signage, or advertising campaign or systematic code enforcement gap.
evidence: 4 illegal posting complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3100% spike, z-score 11.72, highest z-score in dataset)
Highest statistical severity among all spikes, though not most recent
Unsanitary Condition ranks 10th in 90-day volume (329 complaints), indicating broader cleanliness concerns
reporting_angles: Photograph current state of streets in Jackson Heights / Elmhurst for illegal posters, stickers, tags, and unlicensed vendor signs
File FOIL request for 311 location data to map where illegal posting is concentrated—may reveal specific corridors or transit nodes
Contact Department of Environmental Protection and Community Board to ask if there was a known posting campaign or enforcement surge 3 weeks ago

themes_detail.label: Mobile Food Vendor Surge
themes_detail.summary: Mobile food vendor complaints jumped to 8 approximately 2 weeks ago versus a baseline of 1.4 per week—a 482% increase (z-score: 5.96)—suggesting either a sudden influx of unlicensed vendors or enforcement crackdown that sparked resident complaints.
evidence: 8 mobile food vendor complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.4 weekly baseline (482% increase, z-score 5.96)
Jackson Heights is known for food vendor economy; suggests material change in street vending landscape
Community Board budget repeatedly requests SBS (Small Business Services) funding, indicating ongoing vendor-related tensions
reporting_angles: Walk major commercial corridors (Roosevelt Ave, 82nd St, etc.) and catalog vendor presence; compare to prior months if possible
Interview SBS and Parks Department about any recent crackdowns on unlicensed vendors or permit policy changes in the district
Talk to street vendors and residents about what changed 2 weeks ago—did enforcement increase, or did new vendors arrive?

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees and Branches
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints rose to 7 last week versus a baseline of 2.4 per week—a 195% increase (z-score: 4.16)—likely driven by warm weather and spring growth, but may indicate Parks Department maintenance backlog.
evidence: 7 overgrown tree complaints last week vs. 2.4 weekly baseline (195% increase, z-score 4.16)
Community Board repeatedly requests park maintenance funding, indicating chronic resource constraints
Seasonal timing (spring growth) may explain spike, but if sustained into summer suggests staffing or budget issues
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department about tree trimming schedule and whether they are behind on maintenance in CD 403
Identify specific locations via 311 data and photograph overhanging branches or visibility hazards
Cross-reference with community board budget requests to show this is a known, persistent complaint
